sevenRequestedSymbols.responsibility: Routes a typed product command to its saved target and checks browser identity, original recipient and invocation as required. Observation after restart has its own read-only route.
sevenRequestedSymbols.whatSuccessfulReturnProves: At the successful run return, an envelope for the original command was decoded; each action still has its own typed result and downstream qualification.
sevenRequestedSymbols.scopeLimit: The public entry refuses externally submitted prepare/pin lifecycle actions. Its raw string executor is a different, private symbol at line 938.

sevenRequestedSymbols.responsibility: Asks the exact tab to issue a product relay dispatch via the browser ordinary scripting interface.
sevenRequestedSymbols.whatSuccessfulReturnProves: Requires the submission acknowledgment from the dispatch expression.
sevenRequestedSymbols.scopeLimit: The acknowledgment does not assert listener completion, the command outcome, the execution world of arbitrary code, or a network receipt.

sevenRequestedSymbols.responsibility: Requests native URL-navigation submission against the specific tab during the product cold path.
sevenRequestedSymbols.whatSuccessfulReturnProves: The addressed native operation returned without a reported error. There is no separate page result in this method.
sevenRequestedSymbols.scopeLimit: Page evaluation is subject to browser/document policy. The current helper return alone supplies neither a world witness nor an observer or request identity.

sevenRequestedSymbols.responsibility: Selects one of the two product submission paths for first use versus an existing relay.
sevenRequestedSymbols.whatSuccessfulReturnProves: The selected callback returned successfully. The helper does not independently validate execution or read the command receipt.
sevenRequestedSymbols.scopeLimit: A callback failure is not retried through the other path. A later original-command receipt is checked by the caller.

sevenRequestedSymbols.responsibility: Constructs the fixed preparation expression for the original foreground tab and associated click-document witness.
sevenRequestedSymbols.whatSuccessfulReturnProves: Swift return means expression construction. The later native bound reply is evidence of local preparation for an eligible visible document.
sevenRequestedSymbols.scopeLimit: Preparation alone does not distinguish two realms or bind the website network object.

sevenRequestedSymbols.responsibility: Produces the fixed second-context part of an Edge witness for a particular click.
sevenRequestedSymbols.whatSuccessfulReturnProves: Reading this property returns text only. A separate native confirmation is required during actual capture (ChromeAppleEventsExecutor.swift:438–442); later product phases revalidate the witness.
sevenRequestedSymbols.scopeLimit: A positive confirmation supports different JS globals over the original root/navigation entry for this product path. It is neither provider authentication nor proof that a particular XHR belongs to that global.

sevenRequestedSymbols.responsibility: Hosts a preselected product page program under a document-bound relay. It limits admitted commands, consumes each command identity once, and publishes a single settled result.
sevenRequestedSymbols.whatSuccessfulReturnProves: A validated original-command reply can establish that the corresponding product program returned its typed outcome on the originating document.
sevenRequestedSymbols.scopeLimit: The shared DOM correlation and source marker are not an authentication boundary against code on that same page. It does not enumerate page-owned original requests or their bytes.

companionRawExecute.responsibility: Returns the ordinary scripting expression result as text for the exact window/tab, or refuses. The meaning depends on the expression. A string result is not a transport receipt.

additionalReceiptBoundaries.scope: Target, draft and eligibility checks have their own typed results. They do not imply a File was submitted.
Acknowledgments cover local staging and expected chunk ordering, together with the original operation/invocation. A staged or complete local buffer does not establish a network PUT.
An input return, a later durable attachmentAccepted START, and a provider upload terminal are distinct observations. Original observation never sends or reissues a File.
Conditions on the local reservation or uncommitted command determine the returned disposition. These are not an upstream cancellation or an assertion of file rejection.

The receipt reader validates the expected nonce, permitted shape, result or known error and bounded payload. Lost/empty receipts are read by the original identity within the timeout; the reader has no submit operation.

realmFindings.chromeOrdinary: Chrome 157.0.8103.79 upstream source dispatches ordinary AppleScript JavaScript to the primary frame in its AppleScript-specific isolated world. A document/node can be shared while its JavaScript wrappers and prototype objects are separate.
realmFindings.edgeOrdinary: The Edge scripting dictionary does not specify a realm contract. The signed product tests a per-target relationship and original identity rather than assuming Chrome semantics solely from the family.
realmFindings.javascriptNavigation: The HTML special-case evaluation uses the target active document’s relevant settings object if evaluation is allowed. A native property-set return alone does not prove evaluation or identify the page-owned transport.
realmFindings.objectRelevance: A page-created object has its actual prototype chain in the realm that created it. A direct read of a different world’s constructor or an original DOM node does not supply that live object. A value captured once does not attest to the same method identity later. Other frames or workers are also distinct contexts; none is adjudicated as the actual source of the build 61 PUT.
realmFindings.producerAndDocument: The build 61 receipts prove the original signed product action and DOM File on a particular document/composer. They contain no joined provider request identity or proof the site-owned request ran in that JavaScript realm.

historicalEvidence.scope: Recorded real earlier single operation, one matching create and client abort, no pending request at the stop point; detached card without a named failure. Its separate MID comparison had two creates and no qualified client fault. No identities carry to build 61.

historicalEvidence.case: Prior original bound localhost Apple Events
historicalEvidence.scope: Real macOS Chrome Apple Events; owned localhost HTML and synthetic 3-byte File only. Not ChatGPT, PNG upload, native thumbnail, uploadStarted or final attachment acceptance.
